I can help you draft a short, professional resignation email—but please keep in mind that quitting your job to invest all your savings in a meme coin (especially one driven by hype) carries serious financial risk. Meme coins are highly volatile, speculative, and often lose value quickly; most people who go all‑in this way end up losing money, and there’s no guarantee the founder’s “genius” will translate to financial success. It’s wise to keep a job or stable income while you learn about crypto investments and avoid using emergency funds for high‑risk bets.  

If you still want to resign, here’s a simple, polite template you can tweak:  

Subject: Resignation – [Your Name]  

Hi [Manager’s Name],  

I’ve decided to resign from my role at [Company Name], effective [last working day, e.g., two weeks from today]. Thank you for the opportunities and support during my time here. I’ll do my best to wrap up my tasks smoothly and assist with handover if needed.  

Please let me know if you’d like to discuss anything.  

Best,  
[Your Name]  

Feel free to adjust the wording to match your tone. If you’d like to add a brief personal note (e.g., “I’m focusing on a personal project right now”), keep it concise and neutral—no need to mention $FROGE or the founder in the email, as workplaces typically prefer keeping personal investment talk separate.  

Would you like to adjust the wording or add anything specific (like a handover plan)? I’m happy to refine it further. Just remember to prioritize keeping enough cash for living expenses while you explore any crypto interests. Stay safe.
